description: Every tests/v1_programs program that `oracle diff` does not classify MATCH against Forge, and every known difference family of the generated corpora, with its diagnosis, the SPEC rule, the evidence and the owner of the fix. Tracked, not accepted: SPEC-v1 §8.4 and CLAUDE.md principle 2 require 0 POTENTIAL_SILENT_WRONG on the gate corpora, so W4/F1 is not signed off while any POTENTIAL_SILENT_WRONG entry is listed here. Checked against a live oracle by `cargo test -p forge-cli --test oracle_gate -- --ignored` (every other program must be MATCH, each listed one must have exactly its class, and every POTENTIAL_SILENT_WRONG difference of a family program must have the family's signature; with AICAD_ORACLE_GATE_DIRS it also checks generated corpora: every POTENTIAL_SILENT_WRONG difference must have a family signature or belong to a program listed under `generated`); remove an entry in the same change that makes it MATCH.

programs.forge: e2 fails with DEPENDENCY_FAILED: its targets name the failed tag t1 through a `tagged` query, and features referenced by id (sketch, datum, tag, pattern seed) are checked before field expressions and range checks
programs.oracle: INVALID_DISTANCE: the oracle checks the tag only when it resolves the query, after the range check

programs.forge: the join target is geometrically unchanged (the tool equals it): not in `bodies`, info FORGE_BOOLEAN_NO_CHANGE names it
programs.oracle: lists the target in `bodies` as `modified` because the tool is in its component
programs.diagnosis: the SPEC does not say whether an unchanged join target is `modified`; both engines agree on geometry, topology and the part's final bodies
programs.owner: W0 ruling, then W4 (forge-ops/forge-regen) or W7 aligns

programs.forge: tools strictly inside the target: not in `bodies`, info FORGE_BOOLEAN_NO_CHANGE
programs.owner: W0 ruling, then W4 or W7 aligns

programs.forge: the two pieces of e1 re-joined into one body of origin e1: `removed` is empty (the origin survives in `bodies`)
programs.oracle: `removed` = [e1/r.bottom] (the second piece's origin, although it is also the result's origin)
programs.diagnosis: the SPEC does not say whether a join component's other targets that share the kept origin are `merged_into`/`removed`; Forge's reading keeps `removed` disjoint from the result origins
programs.owner: W0 ruling, then W4 or W7 aligns

programs.forge: 10 faces (8 plane, 2 cylinder), 18 edges (12 line, 6 circle), hand-counted and asserted in tests/v1.rs
programs.oracle: 20 edges, 8 circles: two arcs cross OCCT's cylinder seams and stay split at the seam vertex

programs.forge: 7 faces (6 plane, 1 cylinder), 13 edges (10 line, 3 circle), volume in closed form, asserted in tests/v1.rs (the closed-form twin of generated gen1_s41_00138)
programs.oracle: 14 edges, 4 circles: the bottom rim arc passes OCCT's cylinder seam at +x and is split there

programs.forge: the notched hole wall is one cylinder face (6 cylinders, 14 faces, 35 edges), asserted in tests/v1.rs (gen1_s23_01337 reduced)
programs.oracle: 7 cylinders, 15 faces, 37 edges: the wall stays split at OCCT's seam, with its rim arcs
programs.diagnosis: oracle normalization gap (periodic faces split along seams are not re-merged)

programs.forge: 24 edges (22 line, 2 circle), hand-counted and asserted in tests/v1.rs; the notch wall y = 0 meets the hole wall along x = 5, y = 0
programs.oracle: 23 edges (21 line): that edge lies on OCCT's cylinder seam line and is dropped as a seam
programs.diagnosis: oracle normalization bug: an edge between two different faces is a real edge even where it coincides with a seam

programs.forge: the plate is cut by a 0.0005 x 0.01 x 0.01 mm notch (5e-8 mm3; every dimension >= 500 LINEAR_TOLERANCE): modified, 10 faces, 24 edges, asserted in tests/v1.rs
programs.oracle: leaves the plate untouched and unlisted: its `meets` test skips targets whose common volume is below 1e-12 s^3 (here 1.9e-7 mm3)
programs.diagnosis: oracle volume threshold below which real cuts are dropped (the twin of generated gen1_s23_00667)
programs.owner: W7b (oracle); W0 may want to state the smallest cut that counts

programs.forge: 6 bspline edges: the pocket's side walls (vertical planes that miss the ring axis) cut the fillet torus in spiric sections, which are not conics; the horizontal planes' sections are circles (16); asserted in tests/v1.rs
programs.oracle: 4 bspline, 19 circle: GeomConvert at 1e-7 s (s = 120 mm, 1.2e-5 mm) fits short spiric arcs by circles, plus one seam split
programs.diagnosis: oracle curve recognition too loose for short arcs; the SPEC's tolerance `1e-7·s` scales with the body, not with the curve (open W0 wording), and recognition should require an exact conic of the intersection, not a fit

families.signature: an `edges` row where the oracle has 1 or 2 more edges, or an `edge_types` row where only conic types (`circle`, `ellipse`) differ and the oracle has 1 or 2 more of each
families.rule: SPEC-v1 §8.3 rule 1: the same-domain merge re-merges what OCCT split along seams; a circular or elliptic arc that crosses a periodic face's seam must be one edge, as Forge reports it
families.evidence: seam_boss_over_hole and seam_notch_in_disk (hand-counted); 509 of the 517 POTENTIAL_SILENT_WRONG programs of the generated runs below have only rows of this family (1 of them with ellipses, gen1_s5_00051)

families.signature: a `faces` row where the oracle has 1 more face, or a `face_types` row where only periodic types (`cylinder`, `cone`, `sphere`, `torus`) differ and the oracle has 1 more (its rims are oracle-seam-split-arcs rows)
families.rule: SPEC-v1 §8.3 rule 1: periodic faces that OCCT split along seams are re-merged
families.evidence: seam_split_hole_wall_face (gen1_s23_01337 reduced, reproduced); generated gen1_s5_01905, gen1_s23_01337, gen1_s23_01883

families.signature: an `edges` row where Forge has exactly 1 more edge, or an `edge_types` row whose only difference is 1 more `line` in Forge
families.rule: SPEC-v1 §8.3 rule 1 and the v0 seam rule drop seam edges, not real edges between two faces that lie on a seam line
families.evidence: seam_edge_on_hole_seam (hand-counted, reproduced); generated gen1_s5_01279, gen1_s11_01378, gen1_s11_01890 (each has a Forge edge between a hole wall and a cut face on the hole's seam line)

generated.description: `oracle gen --ir v1 --count <n> --seed <s>` corpora diffed on 2026-09-24 against this build (debug aicad): seed 41 x 200 and seeds 5, 11, 23 x 2000. POTENTIAL_SILENT_WRONG outside the families: only the programs listed here, each hand-diagnosed as an oracle-side difference.

programs.diagnosis: the pocket's corner pokes 0.0011 mm out of a hole of e4 (a 0.0014 x 0.0018 x 0.25 mm sliver, 3.2e-7 mm3): Forge cuts it (e4 modified, 11 faces); the oracle's `meets` threshold (1e-6 mm3 at this scale) leaves e4 untouched
the oracle recognizes 2 of the 6 spiric pocket-wall/torus sections as circles (plus one seam-split arc)

generated.robustness: not POTENTIAL_SILENT_WRONG, listed for the MATCH rate: Forge fails revolves of profiles with a rounded corner on the axis with INVALID_RESULT (FORGE_UNBOUNDED_DOMAIN on the degenerate torus face; 10 + 6 + 7 programs with their dependents), one boolean FORGE_BOOLEAN_INCONSISTENT (gen1_s5_01347), and 3 programs whose sketch-on-face probe matches 2 OCCT faces in the oracle's replay (gen1_s5_01098, gen1_s23_00745, gen1_s23_01729)
